correctness.rationale: For two workers/two firms every complete DA matching has exactly one alternative; original weak Pareto domination must use the alternative and requires at least two tied agents (one across each alternative pair), while four ties eliminate strict gain. Independent exhaustive enumeration of all 16 deterministic tie policies and 3^4=81 weak-order profiles gives coefficient pairs (c2,c3)=(1,2) for 10, (2,3) for 4, (3,4) for 2. Every fixed policy has risk c2*t²(1-t)²/4+c3*t³(1-t)/2; convex mixing cannot beat the first class. Equal worker-side priorities attain Pmin=t²(1-t)(3t+1)/4, while independent fair four-agent tie breaks give Pind=t²(1-t)(7t+3)/8. Independently reimplemented complete DA and Pareto test for all 1296 inputs, reproducing exact classes. Polynomial coefficient expression establishes all real 0<=t<=1.
